actions.action: Replace the key-fob onboarding with a hosted first week, pairing every new member with an existing one.
actions.why: Multiple tables described joining as an administrative event rather than a social one.
actions.tension: Asks existing members for unpaid hosting time, which the most active members already say is stretched.

actions.action: Run one cross-day gathering each month so the Tuesday and Thursday communities actually meet.
actions.why: Weekday tribes have formed that never overlap, splitting the membership into parallel communities.
actions.tension: Another recurring commitment in the calendar the programme team says is already too full.

actions.action: Create a member wall of faces and first names at the entrance so regulars can learn who's who.
Host a monthly newcomers' lunch, cooked and hosted by a rotating table of long-standing members.
Hold an exit conversation with every leaving member and share the anonymised reasons with the membership.
Open the ground floor and café to the public on weekdays.
actions.why: The street-facing floor was repeatedly described as the building's front door to new members and neighbours.
actions.tension: Trades away the quiet that a paying segment of the membership explicitly values.

actions.action: Designate the second floor as a protected quiet floor with enforced norms.
actions.why: A distinct group pays precisely for calm and predictability, and feels it eroding.
actions.tension: Requires enforcement nobody currently owns, and shrinks bookable event space.

actions.action: Fix the lift before any new cosmetic work, and publish a repair date the members can hold the board to.
Redesign the entrance so the café, not the key-fob gate, is the first thing a visitor meets.
Audit which doors are locked by default and unlock every one that doesn't genuinely need to be.
Treat the café's deficit as a marketing budget with a cap, not a problem to eliminate.
actions.why: The money table agreed the café is what makes the place worth paying for.
actions.tension: A named, capped subsidy must come from somewhere, most likely the events surplus.

actions.action: Open the café hatch to the street on market days with a short pavement menu.
Move the Monday deep-clean to after hours so the week doesn't start smelling of disinfectant.
Let members run the café one Saturday a month as a pay-what-you-can community kitchen.
Rebuild the pricing tiers around ability to pay, ending legacy discounts for funded organisations.
actions.why: The current tiers were described as subsidising the members who need it least.
actions.tension: Risks losing anchor organisations whose block bookings underwrite the winter months.

actions.action: Publish a plain-language annual budget on one page, income and costs side by side.
Set up a solidarity fund so members can round up their fee to cover a place for someone who can't pay.
Consolidate the three legacy grant reports into one shared quarterly narrative and reclaim the programme manager's time.
Trial a day-pass priced so that three visits cost more than a month of membership.
Hand members the keys: a self-serve process to host their own events with the space's kit.
actions.why: Members repeatedly said they want to host rather than attend, and the best moments were unprogrammed.
actions.tension: Less curatorial control over quality and brand, and more wear on the building.

actions.action: Cancel the two lowest-attended recurring events and leave the slots deliberately empty for member use.
Schedule staff-hosted noticeboard hours that pick up whatever conversation is already happening in the room.
Publish a one-page how-to-host guide covering booking, kit, cleanup, and who to call.
Livestream one flagship event per season for members who can't be in the building.
Name which decisions no longer need everyone: delegate day-to-day calls to staff and reserve member votes for direction.
actions.why: Consensus was named as the way the group avoids deciding; small things get votes, big things get postponed.
actions.tension: Someone must be trusted to decide without everyone, which is exactly what currently feels uncomfortable.

actions.action: Publish board minutes within a week, with decisions and owners highlighted.
Hold a quarterly open-books session where the board walks members through the accounts.
Put the floor-zoning plan to a full membership vote, framed as a six-month experiment with a named review date.
Report back annually on which member proposals were actioned, and by whom.
